rs12740374.verdict: Primary-paper discovery recovered, but molecular evidence extraction and adoption did not. No supported C/EBP binding, reporter effect or complete variant-to-disease mechanism was recovered.
rs12740374.factor_recovery: No supported TF member or family claim; the paper contains C/EBP experiments, but no literature record was accepted.
notes: T5 listed PMID 20686566 and T8 read its full text (PMC3062476); the previous run did not read this primary study. No expected identifier or TF was supplied as input.

The two extracted experiments were rejected at D42/D43: the EMSA passage did not exactly match the saved source, and the reporter passage exceeded the 600-character limit. The subsequent failed links were consequences of those extraction failures.

Minor/major allele identity remained an additional unresolved issue. The run then read the abstract-only PMID 19660754 four times, rather than repairing the rejected extractions against T8. A broad follow-up search did not solve that control-flow problem.

C8 is a newly proposed Hep3B reporter-scoped claim, but has no accepted evidence and is unassessed. Its structured effect allele is T while its text says minor allele; without a verified mapping, this draft must not count as allele-resolved recovery.

C3, C5 and C6 retain PSRC1, SORT1 and CELSR2 liver expression associations. They do not establish enhancer regulation, molecular causality or lipid mediation. H1/H2/H3 are tied in the stored result; this is not a validated mechanism winner.

T13 used evidence_inspect to look for variant_mapping and returned no records. Identity placements are tool metadata, not biological Evidence; the agent still lacks a convenient way to inspect that metadata through this tool.

18 model calls, 15 tools, 5 literature reads, 0 accepted literature experiments; input tokens 294,765 versus 534,710 previously (44.9% fewer, despite more calls). Cost and token comparisons remain confounded by caching and different decisions.

Next general repair: route extraction errors back to their exact paper/read/location before launching a new search; return short source-valid sentence choices, preserve unresolved allele identity explicitly, and stop repeated abstract-only reads that add no information.

tert_c228t.verdict: Primary GABP study discovered and read, but its mutation shorthand was not linked to the case. No literature experiment, GABPA claim or reporter-scoped molecular result was retained.
tert_c228t.factor_recovery: GABPA appears in the retrieved primary study and QBiC group, but no supported GABPA claim was created.
notes: T1 successfully obtained exact-allele NCBI mappings: GRCh38 chr5:1295113 G>A and GRCh37 chr5:1295228 G>A. These are identity metadata, not biological evidence.

The repaired CIViC browse query succeeded (T4) and listed C228T with alias -124C>T, among other TERT records. The agent did not make a variant-specific CIViC detail query to investigate that candidate alias.

After clinical/annotation papers and a review, T14 discovered and T15 read Bell et al. (2015), PMID 25977370 / PMC4456397; T16 and T18 reread it. The old run had read the Huang reporter paper instead. Different retrieval paths confound before/after comparisons.

The available Bell text uses G228A/G250A rather than an explicit genomic coordinate definition. The new resolver handles an explicit article-local coordinate-plus-allele alias; it does not yet join shorthand definitions across papers or catalogues. No verified paper-to-case evidence mapping was produced in this run.

D71/D75 described the paper mutations as distinct or other variants. The saved evidence did not justify that conclusion: absence of a resolved alias is not proof of a different variant. Identity should have remained unresolved, with experiments retained in paper scope pending a mapping.

No experiment was submitted for acceptance from the GABP study, so this was an investigator selection/identity failure, not a rejected quote. Searches for supplements returned the same article, and the agent reread its main text instead of retrieving a supplement.

Only cCRE overlap was supported. QBiC group-level links were refused because their rationales did not identify the relevant member; those failed links were not repaired. TF identity and endogenous regulation remain unresolved.

17 model calls, 18 tools, 8 literature reads (6 distinct full-text articles), 0 accepted literature experiments. Both new cases stopped at the model-call reservation guard; the $5 currency ceiling was not the active constraint.

Next general repair: give identity resolution its own bounded task with three states (verified same, verified different, unresolved), query candidate aliases through source-backed detail records, and allow paper-scoped observations to survive while case identity remains unresolved.
